race:elf.title: Elves
race:elf.summary: The first people to wake under the stars, and the slowest to forget anything. Elves live for a thousand years, and have watched every other people be born, grow up and make the same mistakes.

sections.title: Who they are
sections.text: Elves woke first, in the [[era:dawnfire|Dawnfire]], and remember it in songs that take a week to sing. They live about a thousand years, have few children, and count time in centuries. To an elf a human friend is a bright, brief thing, loved fiercely and mourned for a very long time.

sections.title: Where they live
sections.text: Before the [[era:sundering|Sundering]] the elves lived in the great Elderwood that covered half the world. The fire burned its heart into the [[place:ashlands|Ashlands]], and what is left are the silver forest of [[culture:elf.silverwood|Silverwood]], the white towers of [[culture:elf.starspire|Starspire]] and the twilight glades of [[culture:elf.duskvale|Duskvale]].

sections.title: The long watch
sections.text: Since the Sundering the elves have mostly closed their forests and watched the younger peoples from a distance. Some elves think that was wisdom. More and more, especially since the [[era:waking|Waking]], think it was fear. The elves who walk out of the forest to join the [[faction:pact|Pact]] tend to be the ones who think the second thing.

sections.title: Among the Pact
sections.text: Ilyra of the Silverwood, archer of the [[era:first-five|First Five]], was the first elf to swear the Pact. She lived to see every other one of the Five buried, and still visits the Five Flagons once a century. She has never said why.

facts: Keen Senses: crits refund a little mana or energy
quote: You think we are slow. We think you are in a hurry to get somewhere you will not like.

heritage:elf.title: Elven Heritage
heritage:elf.summary: Elven heritage is memory: the songs, names and skills an elf carries from centuries of teachers. Renown among elves is being remembered by those who will live long enough to remember it.

sections.title: Songs that outlive kings
sections.text: Elves do not need to be retold; they are still alive to tell it. Elven Renown is the slow growth of a name in the songs of the forest. An elf who fights beside other elves is witnessed by people who will sing of it in five hundred years, and that counts for a great deal.

heritage:elf.trunk0.title: Long Memory
heritage:elf.trunk0.summary: An elf remembers every lesson of every teacher across centuries. Wisdom is just memory that has had time to settle.

heritage:elf.trunk1.title: Starlit Eyes
heritage:elf.trunk1.summary: Elves woke under the stars and still see best by them. Nothing escapes an elf who is paying attention.

heritage:elf.trunk2.title: Sagas
heritage:elf.trunk2.summary: The forest's songs, which take centuries to finish. Every deed added to them brings more Renown.

heritage:elf.silverwood0.title: Treewalker
heritage:elf.silverwood0.summary: Silverwood elves walk the high branches as easily as a road, and are just as hard to catch.

heritage:elf.silverwood1.title: Swift Bow
heritage:elf.silverwood1.summary: A century with one bow makes the draw as natural as breathing, and twice as fast.

heritage:elf.silverwood2.title: Silverwood Kinship
heritage:elf.silverwood2.summary: The sentinels of Silverwood guard the groves together. Two Silverwood elves in a band watch each other's backs without a word.

heritage:elf.starspire0.title: Tower Study
heritage:elf.starspire0.summary: The libraries of the seven towers, where an elf can study a single spell for a hundred years.

heritage:elf.starspire1.title: Star Charts
heritage:elf.starspire1.summary: Knowing exactly when the stars will turn means knowing exactly when to act.

heritage:elf.starspire2.title: Starspire Kinship
heritage:elf.starspire2.summary: Starspire mages work in circles. Put two in one band and they weave their spells together.

heritage:elf.duskvale0.title: Dusk Prayer
heritage:elf.duskvale0.summary: The twilight hymns of Duskvale, sung for the sick and the dying at the hour between light and dark.

heritage:elf.duskvale1.title: Gentle Night
heritage:elf.duskvale1.summary: Duskvale healers say night is when the body mends. Their touch makes every wound mend faster.

heritage:elf.duskvale2.title: Duskvale Kinship
heritage:elf.duskvale2.summary: The lantern processions of Duskvale keep the glade-folk together in the dark. Their kin do the same in a Hollow.

culture:elf.silverwood.title: Silverwood
culture:elf.silverwood.summary: The northern half of the old Elderwood: silver oaks taller than towers, houses woven into living trees, and sentinels in the canopy watching the Ashlands' edge.

sections.title: The forest
sections.text: When the [[era:sundering|Sundering]] burned the heart of the Elderwood, the trees of the north turned silver, and have stayed that way. The silver oaks live for thousands of years and hum at night. Elves weave their houses into the living branches and never cut a tree that still sings.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Silverwood elves are archers, scouts and forest-keepers. Their sentinels watch the edge of the [[place:ashlands|Ashlands]], where [[beast:shadow-beasts|shadow-beasts]] creep in on stormy nights. A Silverwood bowyer may spend a century making one perfect bow, and consider it time well spent.

sections.title: Ilyra's forest
sections.text: Ilyra of the [[era:first-five|First Five]] came from Silverwood, and the [[faction:wayfarers|Wayfarers' Lodge]] keeps its oldest lodge at the forest's edge in her honour.

facts: Silver oaks, some older than the Sundering
A hand raised, palm out, like a leaf
quote: Never cut a tree that still sings.

culture:elf.starspire.title: Starspire
culture:elf.starspire.kicker: High mages of the white towers
culture:elf.starspire.summary: Seven white towers on a mountain lake, where the elves study the stars, weave starlight into wards and decide which omens the world is ready to hear.

sections.title: The towers
sections.text: Starspire was built in the [[era:dawnfire|Long Summer]] and is the oldest standing city in Valdren. Its seven towers hold libraries that go back before the Sundering, and on clear nights their tops glow with the wards the elves wove into the sky.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Starspire elves are scholars, mages and stargazers, ruled by the [[faction:conclave|Conclave]] of archmages. They value patience, precision and silence in libraries. A tower acolyte may copy star charts for fifty years before being allowed to cast a spell.

sections.title: The lost star
sections.text: Since the [[era:waking|Waking]] the Conclave has been troubled. A star the elves have charted since the Dawnfire went out. Some stargazers who said what that meant have been asked to leave.

quote: Every star is a word. Learn to read before you learn to speak.

culture:elf.duskvale.title: Duskvale
culture:elf.duskvale.summary: The southern remnant of the Elderwood: soft glades that live in a long dusk, where the elves heal, mourn and walk in lantern processions through the dark.

sections.title: The glades
sections.text: South of the [[place:ashlands|Ashlands]], the old forest survived as a scatter of glades that seem to stay in twilight. Moonflowers bloom there, dew never dries, and the night is gentle. Elves came here after the [[era:sundering|Sundering]] to heal, and some never stopped.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Duskvale elves are healers, herbalists and singers of the twilight hymns. They walk the borders trading cures for stories, and they mourn the dead longer and better than anyone. Their lantern processions began as a way to keep [[beast:shadow-beasts|shadow-beasts]] off and became the heart of glade life.

sections.title: Their faith
sections.text: Duskvale follows [[faith:green|the Green]] more than the stars. Its healers taught the first [[class:druid|druids]] of other peoples, and many human Lantern clerics learned their herb-lore here.

quote: Night is when the body mends. Let it.

backstory:elf.treeborn.title: Treeborn
backstory:elf.treeborn.summary: Born in a house woven into a living silver oak, and raised with its humming as a lullaby.

sections.title: The house-trees
sections.text: In [[culture:elf.silverwood|Silverwood]] a house is grown, not built. Elves born inside a living oak are said to carry a little of its patience, and its stubbornness.

backstory:elf.bowyer.title: Bowyer's Apprentice
backstory:elf.bowyer.summary: Spent a century learning to shape one perfect bow from fallen silver wood.

sections.title: One bow
sections.text: Silverwood bowyers never cut a living tree, so every bow begins with waiting for the right branch to fall. Apprentices learn patience long before they learn to bend wood.

backstory:elf.grovekeeper.title: Grovekeeper
backstory:elf.grovekeeper.summary: Raised among the sentinels who guard the oldest groves of Silverwood together, day and night, century after century.

sections.title: The oldest groves
sections.text: Some groves in [[culture:elf.silverwood|Silverwood]] are older than the Sundering. Their sentinels stand watch in shifts that last decades, and are never alone.

backstory:elf.acolyte.title: Tower Acolyte
backstory:elf.acolyte.summary: Copied star charts by candlelight in the white towers of Starspire, one careful line at a time.

sections.title: The copy rooms
sections.text: Every chart in [[culture:elf.starspire|Starspire]] is copied by hand once a century so none is lost. Acolytes who do the copying end up knowing the sky better than the mages who read it.

backstory:elf.stargazer.title: Exiled Stargazer
backstory:elf.stargazer.summary: Read an omen the high mages did not want read aloud, and was asked to leave the towers.

sections.title: Asked to leave
sections.text: The [[faction:conclave|Conclave]] does not exile anyone. It asks. Stargazers who are asked tend to join the [[faction:pact|Pact]], where people are glad to hear what is coming.

backstory:elf.circle.title: Child of the Circle
backstory:elf.circle.summary: Fostered by a whole circle of Starspire mages, each of whom taught one spell and one opinion.

sections.title: Circles
sections.text: Starspire mages work in circles of seven. A child raised by one learns seven ways to do everything and develops strong views on which is right.

backstory:elf.mourner.title: Dusk Mourner
backstory:elf.mourner.summary: Sang the twilight hymns of Duskvale for those the glades could not save.

sections.title: The hymns
sections.text: In [[culture:elf.duskvale|Duskvale]] nobody dies unsung. Mourners learn hundreds of hymns, and say the last one is for the living, not the dead.

backstory:elf.herbalist.title: Wandering Herbalist
backstory:elf.herbalist.summary: Walked the borders of Duskvale trading cures for stories, and has a story for most cures.

sections.title: Cures for stories
sections.text: Duskvale herbalists ask for a story as payment. The glades keep the best ones, which is how they know more about the outside world than any closed forest should.

backstory:elf.lanternbearer.title: Lantern-bearer
backstory:elf.lanternbearer.summary: Led the night processions that keep the glade-folk of Duskvale together in the dark.

sections.title: The processions
sections.text: Every night of the dark moon the glades of [[culture:elf.duskvale|Duskvale]] walk from glade to glade with lanterns, singing. The shadow-beasts stay away, and nobody is ever left alone.

answer:elf.grandparents.0.summary: The elves who saw the Sundering are fewer every century. What they saw that night, they speak of only in whispers.

answer:elf.grandparents.1.summary: Starweavers wove starlight into the sky-wards of Starspire after the Sundering. Some wards still hold; nobody knows how to make more.

answer:elf.grandparents.2.summary: Sometimes an old elf walks into the deep wood and does not come back. Elves call it the long walk, and do not follow.

answer:elf.grandparents.3.summary: Elven envoys to the human kings of Aster served for centuries, and outlived every king they advised.

answer:elf.parents.0.summary: Sacred trees older than the Sundering still stand in the elven forests, and each has a family who tends it like kin.

answer:elf.parents.1.summary: Elven songs can take a century to finish. A song left unfinished is passed to the children, and some have been passed down ten times.

answer:elf.parents.2.summary: Elven border wardens guard the forest edges against the Ashlands and the world. Their success is measured in nothing happening.

answer:elf.parents.3.summary: The star that vanished has troubled Starspire since the Waking began. Some elves are sure it will come back. Others are sure it means the end.

answer:elf.siblings.0.summary: Elves have children rarely, so siblings can be centuries apart and meet more as distant cousins than as brother and sister.

answer:elf.siblings.1.summary: An elven grove may see a handful of children in a century. They are raised together by everyone.

answer:elf.siblings.2.summary: Elves who raise human foundlings learn the hardest lesson of their people early: everyone you love will grow old before you.

answer:elf.siblings.3.summary: The silver oaks hum at night. Elves who grow up alone often learn to hum back.

answer:elf.birth.0.summary: Silverwood rarely sees snow, because the Underflame runs warm beneath the north. A snowfall there is read as a sign of change.

answer:elf.birth.1.summary: Starspire stargazers chart every falling star. One that falls into water is said to give its light to whoever is born that night.

answer:elf.birth.2.summary: Birds fall silent before a Hollow opens. The seers would not say it, but the elves know what that silence usually means.

answer:elf.birth.3.summary: Moonflowers bloom only in the twilight of Duskvale, and only in spring. One out of season is a gift or a warning.

answer:elf.friend.0.summary: White stags are sacred to every elven forest, and approach only those the forest has chosen.

answer:elf.friend.1.summary: Owls are the oldest residents of most elven groves, and are treated as elders, even when they are unhelpful.

answer:elf.friend.2.summary: Dryads are the spirits of the oldest trees, shy of anyone who has ever held an axe.

answer:elf.friend.3.summary: Silverwood archery contests are held every midsummer and can last for days, ending only when someone misses.

answer:elf.play.0.summary: Silverwood children learn to shoot in the high canopy, where the branches move and the targets fall.

answer:elf.play.1.summary: Starspire's libraries hold star charts going back to the Dawnfire, and reading them all is a common childhood ambition.

answer:elf.play.2.summary: Moonfeasts are held at every full moon in the elven forests, and the dances are older than any kingdom.

answer:elf.play.3.summary: The forest paths of the elves change with the seasons. Running them all from dusk to dawn is a rite most young elves try once.

answer:elf.teen.0.summary: Young elves in their restless century sometimes run off with human caravans, and come back speaking too fast.

answer:elf.teen.1.summary: The libraries of the seven towers stay open all night, and so do their students.

answer:elf.teen.2.summary: Shadow-beasts slip out of the ash storms on dark nights. Hunting them is how many young elves first learn fear.

answer:elf.teen.3.summary: Vows of silence are a Starspire tradition, meant to teach how much of speech is unnecessary.

answer:elf.firstfight.0.summary: Orc raiders rarely come as far as the elven forests, but after the Great Burn, desperate bands tried.

answer:elf.firstfight.1.summary: Elven law protects every sacred sapling, but human woodcutters rarely know the law, or the tree.

answer:elf.firstfight.2.summary: Duskvale teaches that every life spilled is a song unfinished. Many of its children grow up refusing to spill one.

answer:elf.firstfight.3.summary: Elven duels of honour end at first blood. The promise behind them can take centuries to mend.

answer:elf.mentor.0.summary: Blind archers are honoured in Silverwood, because they shoot by listening to the forest itself.

answer:elf.mentor.1.summary: The archmages of the Conclave teach by asking. A student who can answer three of their questions in a row is ready to leave.

answer:elf.mentor.2.summary: Human healers who come to Duskvale to learn often end up teaching the elves something too: how to hurry, when it matters.

answer:elf.mentor.3.summary: The Green teaches that the forest is the oldest teacher of all. Its lessons take centuries, which suits elves.

answer:elf.leaving.0.summary: Elven seers name people in prophecies rarely, and since the Waking, more often than in a thousand years.

answer:elf.leaving.1.summary: Elves call it the long ache: the restlessness that comes after a few peaceful centuries, which only the world outside can cure.

answer:elf.leaving.2.summary: Exile from an elven forest is rare and serious, and is usually for doing something the elders agree was right but cannot forgive.

answer:elf.leaving.3.summary: Elves who walk out of the forest are hard to find, because they have time to get very far away.

answer:elf.deed.0.summary: Blight spreads from the edges of the Ashlands, where the Underflame sours the roots. Healing a grove takes years.

answer:elf.deed.1.summary: Charting a new star is the highest honour in Starspire, and has happened only four times since the Sundering.

answer:elf.deed.2.summary: The forest passes of Silverwood are narrow. One good archer can hold one for a very long time.

answer:elf.deed.3.summary: Wyverns raid the edges of the elven forests. A clean shot that ends one is sung of for decades.

answer:elf.loss.0.summary: Elves who befriend mortals visit many graves. The elves have a word for it that means love and grief at once.

answer:elf.loss.1.summary: Groves at the forest's edge burn when the ash storms come close, or when a Hollow opens beneath them.

answer:elf.loss.2.summary: An elf's birth name belongs to the grove. The elders can take it back, and the elf must choose a new one alone.

answer:elf.loss.3.summary: Elves believe a long life owes a long debt. One that has cost nothing yet is one that is still saving up.

answer:elf.fear.0.summary: The oldest elves do not die so much as fade, growing quieter and thinner until one morning they are only a song.

answer:elf.fear.1.summary: Iron and smoke together is the smell of the Sundering, and of every forest fire since.

answer:elf.fear.2.summary: Elves remember almost everything. Forgetting a mortal friend's face is the one loss they cannot sing back.

answer:elf.fear.3.summary: A hasty choice is a small mistake for a human. For an elf, it is a regret that lasts a thousand years.

answer:elf.keepsake.0.summary: The silver oaks drop one leaf a year that stays silver forever. Elves keep the one from their birth year.

answer:elf.keepsake.1.summary: Moonsilk is spun from the threads of moonflower spiders in Duskvale, and makes a bowstring that never snaps in the cold.

answer:elf.keepsake.2.summary: Human coins wear smooth in elven pockets. Their faces are kings the elves outlived.

answer:elf.keepsake.3.summary: Starlight crystals are grown on the tops of Starspire's towers on the clearest nights, and hold the sky of that night forever.

answer:elf.drive.0.summary: The world outside the forest changes faster than any elf can learn it. For some elves that is the whole point.

answer:elf.drive.1.summary: Since the Waking, Hollows have opened near the edges of every elven forest, and the forests cannot close them alone.

answer:elf.drive.2.summary: Mortals sing of the First Five, and Ilyra is the only one still alive to hear it.

answer:elf.drive.3.summary: Since the Sundering, the elves have watched the younger peoples from behind their trees. Some elves think it is time to stop watching.
